answer:
The **Allegory of Isabella d'Este's Coronation** was created by **Lorenzo Costa the Elder** (c. 1460–1535), NOT "Lorenzo Costa the Younger."

However, to answer your specific question about when the creator died: **Lorenzo Costa the Elder died in 1535** (specifically May 5, 1535, in Mantua).

There is an important distinction here because the Costa family had three generations of painters:
- **Lorenzo Costa the Elder** (c. 1460–1535) - painted the Allegory of Isabella d'Este's Coronation (c. 1505–1506)
- **Ippolito Costa** (1506–1561) - his son
- **Lorenzo Costa the Younger** (1537–1583) - his grandson, died in 1583

So while you asked about "the Younger," it was actually the **Elder** who created this famous painting for Isabella d'Este's Studiolo, and he died in **1535**.

**Lorenzo Costa the Younger** (1537–1583) was an Italian painter of the Renaissance period, active in his native city of Mantua.
Lorenzo was the son of Girolamo Costa and grandson of Lorenzo Costa, and was instructed in the art of painting by his uncle Ippolito. Around 1560, worked in concert with Taddeo Zuccaro in the Belvedere and the Casino of Pope Pius IV at Rome, and died in Mantua in 1583.
Returning to Mantua, he frescoed in the _Sala dello Zodiaco_ in the Ducal Palace. He painted two large altarpieces for _Santa Barbara_ church in the Ducal palace.

The painter who didn't follow the Bentivoglio
Ferrarese and Bolognese school · court painter to the Gonzaga
In 1506 Pope Julius II expelled the Bentivoglio from Bologna — his patrons for twenty years. Costa did not follow them into exile. He moved to Mantua, to the Gonzaga court, and took the place of Andrea Mantegna — who had died that very same year. Loyalty to power, not to people.
Isabella d'Este and Mantegna's unfinished drawing
Isabella d'Este commissioned two paintings for her famous studiolo. One — the Reign of Comus — was based on a drawing left unfinished by Mantegna at his death. Costa completed it. Both are now in the Louvre.
A dynasty of painters
He was the father of the painter Ippolito Costa and grandfather of Lorenzo Costa the Younger. Three generations of brushes in one family — a workshop that outlived its founder by fifty years.

# LORENZO COSTA, KNOWN AS IL VECCHIO · FERRARA, 1460 – MANTUA, 1535 The painter who didn't follow the Bentivoglio Ferrarese and Bolognese school · court painter to the Gonzaga In 1506 Pope Julius II expelled the Bentivoglio from Bologna — his patrons for twenty years. Costa did not follow them into exile. He moved to Mantua, to the Gonzaga court, and took the place of Andrea Mantegna — who had died that very same year. Loyalty to power, not to people. Isabella d'Este and Mantegna's unfinished drawing Isabella d'Este commissioned two paintings for her famous studiolo. One — the Reign of Comus — was based on a drawing left unfinished by Mantegna at his death. Costa completed it. Both are now in the Louvre. A dynasty of painters He was the father of the painter Ippolito Costa and grandfather of Lorenzo Costa the Younger. Three generations of brushes in one family — a workshop that outlived its founder by fifty years. #lorenzocosta #renaissance #mantua #ArtAroundYou #arthistory | Art Around You | Facebook

**Lorenzo Costa the Younger** (1537–1583) was an Italian painter of the Renaissance period, active in his native city of Mantua.
Lorenzo was the son of Girolamo Costa and grandson of Lorenzo Costa, and was instructed in the art of painting by his uncle Ippolito. Around 1560, worked in concert with Taddeo Zuccaro in the Belvedere and the Casino of Pope Pius IV at Rome, and died in Mantua in 1583.
Returning to Mantua, he frescoed in the _Sala dello Zodiaco_ in the Ducal Palace. He painted two large altarpieces for _Santa Barbara_ church in the Ducal palace.

The painter who didn't follow the Bentivoglio
Ferrarese and Bolognese school · court painter to the Gonzaga
In 1506 Pope Julius II expelled the Bentivoglio from Bologna — his patrons for twenty years. Costa did not follow them into exile. He moved to Mantua, to the Gonzaga court, and took the place of Andrea Mantegna — who had died that very same year. Loyalty to power, not to people.
Isabella d'Este and Mantegna's unfinished drawing
Isabella d'Este commissioned two paintings for her famous studiolo. One — the Reign of Comus — was based on a drawing left unfinished by Mantegna at his death. Costa completed it. Both are now in the Louvre.
A dynasty of painters
He was the father of the painter Ippolito Costa and grandfather of Lorenzo Costa the Younger. Three generations of brushes in one family — a workshop that outlived its founder by fifty years.
